subject.title: PR1/6 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt any shared residual durable-runtime boundary beyond the existing task, Task Flow, subagent, delivery, session, restart, and state owners?
rationale: The branch is intentionally documentation-only and contains no mechanical defect to repair, but it asks the project to accept a new core persistence and orchestration direction that current roadmap guardrails do not decide automatically.

options.title: Decline the shared layer for now
options.body: Do not merge this RFC or its implementation series; require concrete narrow gaps to be solved through existing lifecycle owners unless future roadmap priorities change.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowly bounded core design
options.body: Accept a named residual fact that existing owners cannot express, then require a maintained API, migration, compatibility, and proof plan before implementation review.

options.title: Move the proposal to a design discussion
options.body: Keep the RFC out of source documentation while maintainers decide the boundary in a discussion before considering a smaller sponsored PR.

recommendation.title: Decline the shared layer for now
recommendation.body: Do not merge this RFC or its implementation series; require concrete narrow gaps to be solved through existing lifecycle owners unless future roadmap priorities change.

likelyOwner.reason: Their documented overlap with Docs, Agent Reliability, and Runtime Hardening makes them the best available routing candidate, though direct ownership history was not established.
